teaser.text: PepsiCo is a food-and-drink company whose familiar brands turn everyday eating and drinking into a large, repeat-purchase business. To understand how a dollar comes in and goes out, follow the product from brand and factory to customer, shelf and final sale.

stock.title: PepsiCo stock forecast
stock.meta_description: PepsiCo stock forecast: weighted scenarios, recovery drivers, free cash flow and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: PepsiCo’s weighted scenario reaches US$167.75 in October 2027 and US$186.33 in October 2029. It hinges on restoring profitable volume while protecting margin.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains PepsiCo’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could PepsiCo's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: PepsiCo’s weighted forecast reaches US$167.75 in October 2027 and US$186.33 in October 2029, implying a 60% dividend-inclusive return over three years if profitable volume recovery, margin stabilization and stronger cash generation arrive.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for PepsiCo's base case, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Margins are the second major swing factor. Base net margin rises from 11.4% to 12.0%. Bear margin falls from 10.4% to 9.4%. Bull margin rises from 11.7% to 12.8%. The cautious base path reflects the latest 35-basis-point core-margin contraction and the North American food pressure caused by affordability spending and marketing. Separate charges decline from $500 million to $150 million in the base case, while the bear retains $250 million and the bull reaches zero.

blocks.heading: How much cash does PepsiCo really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation is not an immediate cash payment, but it gives employees something valuable and can dilute shareholders. Deducting it, along with payments to minority owners, leaves less cash for PepsiCo’s shareholders. Dividends absorbed nearly all of that adjusted amount. Cash generation is therefore strong, but the margin for debt reduction, acquisitions or reinvestment is narrow.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for PepsiCo today?

paragraphs.text: A trailing P/E compares the share price with past-year earnings; a forward P/E compares it with an estimate. The forward measure looks cheaper only if forecast earnings arrive. Profit can also rise because PepsiCo charges more while shoppers buy fewer bags of chips or drinks, so volume and pricing must be read together.

dividend.title: PepsiCo dividend: cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: PepsiCo dividend history, cash coverage, plans and yield explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: In 2025, PepsiCo paid a US$5.62 dividend per share, while free cash flow after stock pay was US$5.76 per share. Real free cash flow after stock pay was US$7,379 million against US$7,638 million of dividends.
dividend.closing: The full PepsiCo memo also examines PepsiCo’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does PepsiCo pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends remain resilient but do not fully solve the cash constraint. FY2026 dividend per share is $5.81, based on two payments of $1.4225 and two of $1.48. The base reaches $6.53 by FY2029 through increases near 4%. The bear reaches $6.22 through 2% increases. The bull reaches $6.73 through stronger increases. PepsiCo has raised its dividend for 54 consecutive years, but distributions exceeded real free cash flow in recent years, so a cut is less likely than slower growth.

blocks.heading: Is PepsiCo's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: - **Cash for investment and returns** — Capital spending, dividends and acquisitions compete for cash. The company’s real free cash flow after stock pay was US$7,379 million in 2025, against US$7,638 million of dividends.
